title: Safety-net routing and graceful deprecation strategy for pinned model versions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Define and implement a safety-net routing layer and deprecation workflow for user-pinned model versions that minimizes customer impact and preserves predictable SLAs. This ticket covers the policy model, runtime routing changes, telemetry/alerts, and an operational playbook for sunsetting pinned versions across regions and model variants.

Why this exists: Customers pin models to an exact version for reproducibility and compliance. When a pinned version becomes unavailable (hardware failure, security patch, or planned retirement), we must route requests in a deterministic, auditable way that: (1) avoids silent correctness regressions, (2) exposes clear signals to customers and SREs, and (3) supports gradual deprecation with per-customer grace windows.

Key constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: Automatic transparent model substitution without explicit rule/config (we allow opt-in policies).
- Constraint: Must interoperate with existing pin metadata and rollout APIs.
- Constraint: No user-visible latency regression >20% for P99 in failover path for Dedicated customers at P0 SLA.

Unique aspects of this design: introduce the "variant-bridge" concept (an explicit compatibility mapping between a pinned version and acceptable substitute variants), the "sunset corridor" (time-limited grace window configurable per customer/project), and a lightweight signal taxonomy (soft-failure, hard-failure, controlled-deprecate) used by routing decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy engine supports three signals: soft-failure, hard-failure, controlled-deprecate
Per-customer pin config includes: allowed_variants (list), sunset_corridor_days (int), notify_level (none|banner|email)
Failover path executes: pinned -> allowed_variant -> regional-equivalent -> global-compatible -> fail-fast, with observable traces at each hop
SLO/latency regression measured and documented for hosted and dedicated customers; automated canary validates correctness on 5% traffic before 100% switch
Operational playbook created and linked; runbook validated in staged outage test
implementation_notes:
Runtime changes: add a routing policy evaluator that consumes pin metadata and health signals (node health, model-serving status, security flags). Implement 'variant-bridge' table stored in model registry: keys = pinned version, values = ordered acceptable substitutes with compatibility tags and degradation score.

Compatibility scoring: numeric 0-100 used to prefer higher-fidelity substitutes when multiple variants available. Routing algorithm: 1) check pinned instance health; 2) if soft-failure and allowed_variants non-empty, pick highest-score available variant in same region; 3) if none, attempt regional-equivalent (same model family, quantization diff) with degrade marker; 4) as last option use global-compatible variant and attach 'downgrade' metadata to response and traces.

Tech tasks: modify model-registry API (add allowed_variants field), extend routing engine, instrument trace tags (pin_status, chosen_variant, degrade_score), add database migration for per-customer sunset_corridor, and add console UI for per-pin policies.

Backward compatibility: if no allowed_variants set, default to strict fail-fast for pinned hosted customers and to regional fallback for Dedicated customers depending on tenant tier.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Canary): Feature flag enabled in us-west-2 serving cluster only. Route 5% of traffic for internal test tenants; verify P50/P95/P99 and correctness via golden prompts.

Phase 1 (Beta): opt-in tenant UI in Console + API field; invite ~10 customers to enable variant-bridge; run for 2 weeks.

Phase 2 (Gradual): enable automatic safety-net for Dedicated customers with sunset_corridor default 14 days; 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks if no regressions. Hosted customers remain strict unless they opt into allowed_variants.

Rollforward / rollback criteria: Rollforward when golden-prompt top-k exactness delta < 2% and error rate stable. Rollback immediately if error rate increases >1.5x or P99 latency regresses >25% for 10 minutes. Manual override available via Console emergency toggle.
test_plan: Simulate soft-failure: mark node degraded; assert routing picks allowed_variant in-region and attaches degrade_score and reason in trace
Simulate hard-failure: entire region down; assert route to regional-equivalent or global-compatible and alerting triggered
Customer grace window test: create pin with sunset_corridor 7 days and verify notification schedule and auto-cutover after corridor expires
Load test: measure P99 latency on failover path for Dedicated GPU pools and ensure <20% regression
